What pops up in the next four seconds either gets you the call Wednesday morning… or hands the job to Mike from down the road.

No monthly fee. No hosting bill buried in fine print like those other pricks pull. Yours.

Link's below. Take a look. Then book 10 minutes with me and I'll hand you the login.

sequences.subject: Mike still owes you
sequences.email_body:
{{custom_fields.body_opener_inline}}your head's a goddamn mess right now.

Not in a bad way — in the way any guy running a shop off his phone knows too well. Three callbacks you keep meaning to make. A gas station receipt in your pocket with somebody's number on it. Mike still owes you for the water heater. And you're trying to remember all of it while you're elbow deep in someone else's drain.

I've got something that takes it out of your head.

One place for {{company_name}} to live. Every call, every text, every job, every callback — all sitting on your phone.

You do clean work. Time your shop ran clean too.

It's free. Link's below. Website's in there. So is this.

{{custom_fields.landing_url}}

— Kurt

P.S. No contracts. No credit card. Just go see.

sequences.subject: Re: Inquiry — {{company_name}}
sequences.email_body:
I'm tired, slightly annoyed, and disappointed in myself for not making this easier on you.

Two weeks ago I built {{company_name}} a website. Free. Yours.

No card. No contract. No monthly anything. The site, the hosting — all of it, no strings.

And the only thing standing between you and the login was 10 minutes on the phone with me. Any hour. Any day.

And I'm sitting here two weeks later wondering what I missed…

Maybe my emails got buried.

Maybe life just got in the way. Shit happens.

Maybe the offer just sounds too good to be true.

I don't know. I just know it's real. The link still works.

{{custom_fields.landing_url}}

— Kurt

sequences.subject: a man of his word
sequences.email_body:
{{custom_fields.body_opener_inline}}{{custom_fields.deadline_date}}. The last day free is on the table.

Honestly… whether you take it or not doesn't matter to me. It's just code on my computer. It's not like I'm making money from it anyway.

I'm not trying to corner you either — a yes is a small 10-minute risk on something free. A no is keeping your dashboard stacked with sticky notes like a line cook.

It is what it is.

It's all done for you.

You don't have to understand anything.

Just answer questions about the business that you run.

Have a little trust… a man can still be a man of his word.

{{custom_fields.landing_url}}

Have a good one.

— Kurt

P.S. No catch. No fine print. Delete at midnight.
